concept.name: Market peg order
concept.definition: A pegged order whose working price tracks the opposite side of the market: a buy market peg follows the national best offer, a sell market peg follows the national best bid, typically with an offset to stay slightly less aggressive. It behaves like a continuously adjusted marketable limit order.
concept.intuition: It is 'keep me at the ask so I can buy (or at the bid so I can sell) as the market moves' - aggressive but price-bounded.
concept.mechanics: The venue re-prices the order off the contra-side NBBO quote (Cboe ExecInst P: peg Buy to NBO, Sell to NBB) with an optional offset, executing immediately if marketable and re-pegging as the quote moves, bounded by a cap limit price.
concept.formula: Buy working price = national best offer - offset; sell working price = national best bid + offset (bounded by the cap limit price).
concept.failure_modes: It removes liquidity and pays the spread repeatedly as the quote steps away, so total cost can approach that of chasing with market orders. A one-tick-wide or flickering quote can also produce a string of small fills at worsening prices.
concept.misconceptions: Market peg is the opposite reference of primary peg - traders routinely invert the two. It does not guarantee full execution: once the quote moves beyond the cap, the remainder stops following.
concept.example: NBBO is $15.00 x $15.02; your market-pegged buy (offset $0.00) works at $15.02 and takes the offer; when the offer moves to $15.03, the order follows, up to your cap.

citations.source: Cboe Titanium U.S. Equities BOE Specification
citations.section: ExecInst P = Market Peg (peg Buy to NBO, Sell to NBB)
